learn.hook: Different languages, clothes and foods, but one big family! Who are we?
points: The lesson 'We Are All Indians' is about how people in India are different, yet one.
People in India speak many languages, wear many kinds of clothes and eat many foods.
We are different in many ways, but we live together as friends.
'Unity in diversity' means being one, even when we are different.

example.q:
Read this.
In our class there are children from many states.
Anjali speaks Tamil. Gurpreet speaks Punjabi.
Joy speaks Bengali. Meera speaks Marathi.
We eat different foods and wear different clothes.
But we all study, play and laugh together.
We are all Indians!
Which language does Meera speak?
steps: Find Meera's name in the passage.

learn.reallife: Your class may have friends who speak different languages at home. You all learn and play together!

games.title: True or false? (about the class)
items: In the passage, Anjali speaks Tamil.
In the passage, all the children speak the same language.
They speak Tamil, Punjabi, Bengali and Marathi.
In the passage, the children study and play together.
The passage says: 'we all study, play and laugh together.'
People in India speak many languages.
India has many languages, like Hindi, Tamil, Bengali and Marathi.
Being different means we cannot be friends.
We can be different and still be good friends.

items.text: We all study, play and ___ together.

quiz.q: Passage: 'Anjali speaks Tamil.' Which language does Anjali speak?
quiz.explain: The passage says Anjali speaks Tamil.
steps: The question asks which language Anjali speaks.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the children and their languages

quiz.q: Passage: 'Joy speaks Bengali.' Who speaks Bengali?
quiz.explain: The passage says Joy speaks Bengali.
steps: The question asks who speaks Bengali.
quiz.mistake: Does not read whose name goes with the language

quiz.q: Passage: 'But we all study, play and laugh together.' What do the children do together?
quiz.explain: The passage says they study, play and laugh together.
steps: The question asks what the children do together.
Read: 'But we all study, play and laugh together.'
quiz.mistake: Does not read the line carefully

options: Being one, even when we are different
quiz.explain: Unity means being one. Diversity means being different. We are one, even when we are different.
steps: So we are one, even when we are different.
Answer: Being one, even when we are different
quiz.mistake: Thinks being one means being the same

quiz.q: Passage: 'We are all Indians!' What is the same about all these children?
quiz.explain: Their languages, foods and clothes are different, but they are all Indians.
steps: The children have different languages, foods and clothes.
So the same thing is that they are all Indians.
quiz.mistake: Picks something that is different for each child

quiz.q: Your new classmate speaks a different language at home. What is a kind thing to do?
options: Ask them to teach you a word
Tell them to stop speaking it
quiz.explain: Learning a word from a friend shows respect and makes you closer.
steps: Your classmate speaks a different language.
Asking them to teach you a word shows respect.
Laughing or not talking to them is not kind.
Answer: Ask them to teach you a word
quiz.mistake: Does not show respect for a different language

teach.ask: Gappu: My friends speak different languages and eat different food. Are we still one?
teach.praise: Yes! We are different in many ways, but we are all one. We are all Indians!
teach.nudge: Are we all the same, or different? What joins us together?

revise.summary: People in India speak many languages, wear many kinds of clothes and eat many foods. We are different, yet we live together as friends.
focus: Find which child speaks which language in a passage.
remember: 'Unity in diversity' means being one, even when we are different.
Unity means being one. Diversity means being different.
traps: Being one does not mean being the same.
Don't mix up the children and their languages.

learn.hook: Vanakkam! Namaskar! Sat Sri Akal! Hello in many languages!
points: India has many states. Many states have their own main language.
Tamil Nadu – Tamil. Kerala – Malayalam. Karnataka – Kannada.
West Bengal – Bengali. Gujarat – Gujarati. Punjab – Punjabi. Maharashtra – Marathi.
Hindi is spoken in many states, like Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Rajasthan.
Many people in India speak two or more languages.

example.q: Riya is going to visit her cousin in Gujarat. Which language will she hear the most there?
steps: The main language of Gujarat is Gujarati.
The names sound alike: Gujarat → Gujarati.

learn.reallife: Look at an Indian currency note. The amount is written in many Indian languages!

quiz.q: The main language of Kerala is ___.
quiz.explain: People in Kerala mostly speak Malayalam.
steps: The question asks the main language of Kerala.
People in Kerala mostly speak Malayalam.
Tamil is for Tamil Nadu. Kannada is for Karnataka.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the languages of the southern states

quiz.q: Kannada is the main language of which state?
quiz.explain: Kannada is the main language of Karnataka.
steps: Kannada is the main language of one state.
quiz.mistake: Does not link Kannada with Karnataka

quiz.q: Hindi is spoken in many states. Which of these is one of them?
quiz.explain: Hindi is the main language of Uttar Pradesh.
steps: Hindi is spoken in many states.
Hindi is the main language of Uttar Pradesh.
Kerala, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal have other main languages.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every state speaks Hindi as its main language

quiz.q: Odia is the main language of which state?
quiz.explain: Odia is the main language of Odisha.
steps: Odia is the main language of one state.
quiz.mistake: Does not notice that Odia and Odisha sound alike

quiz.explain: Punjabi is the main language of Punjab.
steps: The question asks what people in Punjab mostly speak.
Punjabi is the main language of Punjab.
quiz.mistake: Does not link the state with its language

quiz.q: Marathi is the main language of which state?
quiz.explain: Marathi is the main language of Maharashtra.
steps: Marathi is the main language of one state.
quiz.mistake: Does not link Marathi with Maharashtra

teach.ask: Gappu: Does everyone in India speak the same language?
teach.praise: Wow! India has many states and many languages, like Tamil, Hindi and Bengali!
teach.nudge: Do all states have the same language? Can you name some languages?

revise.summary: India has many states, and many states have their own main language. Hindi is spoken in many states, and many people speak two or more languages.
focus: Match each state with its main language.
Use sound clues: Gujarat → Gujarati, Odisha → Odia.
remember: Tamil Nadu – Tamil. Kerala – Malayalam. Karnataka – Kannada.
West Bengal – Bengali. Gujarat – Gujarati. Punjab – Punjabi. Maharashtra – Marathi.
traps: Not every state speaks Hindi as its main language.
Don't mix up the languages of the southern states.

topics.title: Symbols and festivals that join us

learn.hook: One flag, one anthem, and festivals all year round! What do we share?
points: Our national flag has three colours: saffron on top, white in the middle and green at the bottom.
A navy blue wheel called the Ashoka Chakra is in the middle. It has 24 spokes.
Our national anthem is 'Jana Gana Mana'. National bird: peacock. National animal: tiger.
We celebrate Independence Day on 15 August and Republic Day on 26 January.
Harvest festivals: Pongal in Tamil Nadu, Onam in Kerala, Bihu in Assam, Baisakhi in Punjab.

example.q: Our flag has three colours in bands. Which colour is at the bottom?
steps: The middle band is white, with a navy blue wheel.

learn.reallife: On 15 August and 26 January, schools hoist the flag and sing 'Jana Gana Mana' together.

games.title: Our flag
games.prompt: Put the flag colours in order, from top to bottom

quiz.q: Which colour is at the top of our national flag?
quiz.explain: The top band of the flag is saffron.
steps: Our flag has three bands: saffron, white and green.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the order of the flag colours

quiz.q: What colour is the Ashoka Chakra in the middle of the flag?
quiz.explain: The Ashoka Chakra is a navy blue wheel.
steps: The Ashoka Chakra is the wheel in the middle of the flag.
It is a navy blue wheel.
quiz.mistake: Does not remember the colour of the wheel

quiz.q: How many spokes does the Ashoka Chakra have?
steps: The Ashoka Chakra is a wheel with spokes.

quiz.q: What is the national bird of India?
quiz.explain: The peacock is our national bird.
steps: The question asks for India's national bird.
The peacock is our national bird.
quiz.mistake: Picks a common bird instead of the national bird

quiz.q: When do we celebrate Independence Day?
quiz.explain: India became free on 15 August 1947. We celebrate it every year.
steps: We celebrate Independence Day on that date every year.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up Independence Day and Republic Day

quiz.q: Onam is a harvest festival of which state?
quiz.explain: Onam is the harvest festival of Kerala.
steps: It is the harvest festival of Kerala.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the harvest festivals of different states

teach.ask: Gappu: What things do ALL Indians share, even if they speak different languages?
teach.praise: Jai Hind! We share one flag, one anthem and our national days!
teach.nudge: What flies high on 15 August? What song do we all sing together?

revise.summary: Our flag, national anthem, national bird and animal, national days and harvest festivals join us as one India.
focus: Know the flag colours in order and the Ashoka Chakra.
Know our national symbols and national days.
Match each harvest festival with its state.
remember: Flag: saffron on top, white in the middle, green at the bottom. Navy blue Ashoka Chakra with 24 spokes.
National anthem: 'Jana Gana Mana'. National bird: peacock. National animal: tiger.
Independence Day: 15 August. Republic Day: 26 January.
Pongal: Tamil Nadu. Onam: Kerala. Bihu: Assam. Baisakhi: Punjab.
traps: Don't mix up Independence Day and Republic Day.
Don't mix up the order of the flag colours.
